rationale: The candidate reads as a single compact mass with one dominant cut/notch logic, so it passes the basic program gate for neighborhood living. The four views are consistent enough, and there is no visible self-collision or view-dependent contradiction. The parcel response is decent: the mass sits within the green boundary and the plan shape is oriented coherently rather than merely filling the box. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged by the notch/opening, but the ground response is still modest; the public void is legible in plan yet not fully articulated as a robust threshold or court. The silhouette is coherent but somewhat generic and box-led, with the notch doing more of the work than the overall section. Compared with references, it resonates most with the compact courtyard/multi-volume neighborhood language, but it is less spatially generous and less sectionally expressive than the strongest precedents.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is much larger and more pluralized than the candidate; transfer only the courtyard/hierarchy logic, not the towered composition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like mixed-use aggregation can still read as one public-facing mass when a central void organizes multiple volumes.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is more compact and box-like; do not imitate the glazed perimeter or landscape-heavy setting.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise elongated massing with a strong courtyard/atrium and site-responsive spread suits neighborhood-facing programs.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more fragmented and layered than the candidate; use it as a void-and-bridge precedent, not as a direct form model.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking wings and a large central void can create a legible public interior and clear mass hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This counterfactual leans much more strongly into terraces and sloped roofs than the candidate; useful only as a reminder that section must do program work, not as a copy target.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A stepped or roof-profiled section can support neighborhood living when the section has a clear public/terrace consequence.

warnings: The frontage response is present but still thin; a deeper public threshold or carved court would better match the semantic brief.
Sectional expression is limited; the current form is plausible, but the roof/section does not strongly communicate occupied terrace or daylight logic.
The mass is close to too_box_like; it is saved by the cut/notch and plan coherence.
